title: Building Malchus: how a feeling becomes speech, and speech a world
overview:
*Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the world of speech, the last *hei*. Before the *nesira* it was only the back of *Zeir Anpin*; then each of its *sefiros* is built from the *Malchus* of the matching *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin*, the point where a feeling becomes a felt *yesh*. *Zeir Anpin* is the *tzelem*, the original; *Malchus* is the *dmus*, its print, like the Rebbe on video, a voice over the phone or a copy of the Mona Lisa: the same for what it carries, not the same as a thing. In speech a feeling becomes a separate thing, so the anger a man wants to express is heard in his voice.

To be built, *Malchus* first becomes a point: to speak, first be silent and think, and people will listen. Then it is face to face with *Zeir Anpin*, a speech fully written inside; beyond that its *Malchus*, practiced before the mirror, breaks through the screen and moves the listeners in *Beriya*. This is the large *dalet* of *echad*, built by *chachma* and *bina* and sent out to rule; poor, *dal*, with nothing of its own, rooted in *chesed*.

sections.title: Malchus of Atzilus, the world of speech, sawn from the back of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the world of speech, the last *hei* of the Name. Before the *nesira* it was part of the back of *Zeir Anpin*; after it, each *sefira* of *Malchus* is built from the *Malchus* of the matching *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin*, the point where a feeling becomes a felt *yesh*.

phrases.he: (מז) ומעתה יש להבין בבחינת המלכות דאצילות שנקרא עולם הדבור, בחינת רחל, עלמא דאתגליא, אימא תתאה, והוא ה"א אחרונה דשם יהו״ה (כידוע בענין כאמה בתה, דה"א עילאה דבינה אוזיפת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך לברתא, בחינת ה' מוצאות הפה דדבור כנזכר לעיל) ונקרא מאמר פתוח, כמו ויאמר אלהי״ם, וכמו שכתוב בדבר ה' שמים כו', ועל זה אמר מלכותו בכל כו' כידוע

blocks.text: Going over the chapter at the end of the next class: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is *Rachel*, *alma d'isgalya* (the revealed world), and the last *hei* of the Name. Why the upper one and the lower one are both called *hei*: among other reasons, the one given here is that *bina* lends the five *gevuros*, *mantzepach*, to *Malchus*. So that's a *hei* and that's a *hei*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the review of the chapter at the end of the next class (226); the class reads these lines with no comment of its own.

phrases.he: דהנה ידוע בענין הנסירה שד"ו פרצופין היו כו', דהיינו שבחינת המלכות היתה כלולה בבחינת אחוריים דזעיר אנפין, כמו שכתוב עצם מעצמי כו', כי מאיש לוקחה זאת כו' ואחר הנסירה נבנית המלכות בבנין פרצוף בפני עצמו באורות וכלים, כמו שכתוב ויבן יהו״ה אלהי״ם את הצלע כו'. וביאור הדברים ידוע בזהר ועץ חיים בכמה דוכתי, דהמלכות נקרא עשירית כי נלקחה מעשיראה דכל עשר ספירות דזעיר אנפין, דהיינו מבחינת מלכות של כל ספירה דזעיר אנפין כמו מבחינת מלכות דחכמה דזעיר אנפין נמשך בחינת חכמה דמלכות, ומבחינת מלכות דחסד דזעיר אנפין נמשך חסד דמלכות כו', ועל דרך זה נבנו כל עשר ספירות דמלכות

blocks.text: Then the *nesira* (the sawing apart): *Malchus* was included in the *achoraim* (the back) of *Zeir Anpin*, and from the *Malchus* of each *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin* came that *sefira* of *Malchus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the review of the chapter at the end of the next class (226); the class reads these lines with no comment of its own.

phrases.he: וביאור בחינת מלכות דט' ספירות דזעיר אנפין ידוע, שהוא בחינת ההתגלות של כל מדה וספירה כשבאה בבחינת גלוי ליש ודבר מה במציאת ניכרת כו' כמו מדת אהבה כשבאה בגלוי יש כו'

blocks.text: The *Malchus* of each of the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin* is where the attribute comes out as a *yesh*, a something that is noticed: love, when it comes out as a felt thing. That is the *Malchus* of it. The feeling comes into a sort of *osios* (letters), and a person knows what it is he is feeling.

In the review: the *Malchus* of a *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin* is how the *sefira* comes into revelation as a *yesh*, a thing that is noticed, as above at *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule), where it is engraved and becomes a revealed *yesh*. A person loves something, or hates it, or is angry; often the feeling is still vague. Its *Malchus* is where he says to himself, so to speak, "I love this thing," or "I'm angry": that gives the feeling its *yeshus*. And from that inner expression, the *Malchus* of the *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin*, comes that *sefira* of *Malchus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the review of the chapter at the end of the next class (226); the class reads these lines with no comment of its own.

sections.title: Tzelem and dmus: the original and its copy
sections.summary: *Zeir Anpin* is the *tzelem*, the form itself; *Malchus* is the *dmus*, the print the seal leaves, like the Rebbe on video or a voice over the telephone. For what it carries the copy makes no difference; as a thing it is not the original, like a copy of the Mona Lisa.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת ההתגלות הזאת העצמיות נקרא צלם וצורה העצמית, כציור העצמי דחותם וכהאי גוונא, וכן ציור הפנים עצמו כו' והיינו בחינת הכלים דזעיר אנפין, שעל זה אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד,
שהוא כענין הגבול בכח
phrases.en: It's not the actual *gvul*: the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin* is not the actual *gvul* but a power for the *gvul*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב למעלה (באות כ"ט)

blocks.text: This self-revelation is called the *tzelem* (image) and the essential form, like the essential form of a *chosam* (seal), and the form of the face itself. It is the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*, of which it says "He and His organs are one": like the limit in potential, **not the actual *gvul* but a power for the *gvul***.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת דמות בנוקבא דזעיר אנפין, שנקרא דמות כבוד יהו״ה דזעיר אנפין כידוע בענין נעשה אדם בצלמינו כדמותינו, דצלם בדכורא ודמות בנוקבא כו' והיינו ענין אתוון אתגליפו כו', שהוא בחינת התגלות להתגלות כאותיות החותם הנחקק בשעוה וכהאי גוונא כו'

blocks.text: But the *dmus* (likeness) is in the *Nukva* of *Zeir Anpin*: in "Let us make man in our *tzelem*, after our *dmus*", the *tzelem* is in the male and the *dmus* in the female. This is the engraved letters, a revelation of a revelation: the seal presses its letters into the next level. The *tzelem* is the mold; the *dmus* is the letter it prints.

blocks.title: The Rebbe on video
blocks.text: The *dmus* is exactly like the original, but only a likeness. The Rebbe had his form, his *tzelem*. A video of the Rebbe is not really him: it is a *dmus*. Yet the *dmus* is exactly like the *tzelem*; a video talks and everything, and it is almost like *mamash* seeing the Rebbe. But really it is a *dmus*.

blocks.title: A voice over the telephone
blocks.text: Speech is like a *dmus*: it only comes out from the inner *middos*. But the voice itself, apart from the *middos*, has its own *tzelem*, its own form, and it gets engraved into the telephone. A listener in Los Angeles is not hearing his voice at all; it does not carry that far. He hears a reconstruction, a *dmus*: the voice is turned into another kind of letter, electrical impulses, and the phone set at the other end turns the electricity back into airwaves.

So it is a *dmus* of a *dmus* of a *dmus*, because the voice itself is a *dmus* of the *tzelem* in the emotions and the intellect. That is why *Malchus* is called a *dmus*. Yet it makes no difference: for all intents and purposes the listener might as well be hearing the actual voice. It is like the letters of a seal pressed into the wax.

In the review: the *tzelem* is the essential form, in the male, and the *dmus* is in the female. *Zeir Anpin* is the *tzelem*, still part of the actual form of the thing; speech is only a *dmus* of it. In the voice you hear the love or the anger, but not the *etzem* of the love or the anger, only a *dmus*. And, as was said, being a *dmus* makes no difference, as with the Rebbe on a video.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the review of the chapter at the end of the next class (226); the class reads these lines with no comment of its own.

blocks.title: The Mona Lisa and the Bill of Rights
blocks.text: One thing was left out: in some ways it does make a difference. A *dmus* of the Mona Lisa can be exactly like the original, but it is not worth a hundred million dollars, because it is not the original, no matter what you say. (Some forgeries are so good that they are worth a lot themselves; it doesn't matter.) A copy of the American Constitution or the Bill of Rights carries the whole idea exactly as the original does, but the original document would be worth millions and millions of dollars, and the copy is not. From one side it is exactly the same; from the other, it is not. That is why it is only a *dmus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Added in the review at the end of the next class (226), to the tzelem and dmus of these lines.

blocks.text: This is also *Atik*: *Atik* means a *he'etek*, a copy of the *ratzon ha'atzmi* (the essential will), and the copy comes through by way of *Malchus*. From one side the very same thing is given over; from the other it is only a copy, no longer the original.
blocks.outOfPlace: Added in the review at the end of the next class (226).

blocks.title: The Xerox machine
blocks.text: By the way, this too is a matter of *Malchus*: the letters and the *dmus* let a thing be carried from place to place without the actual intellect. Put this book on a Xerox machine and it makes another copy. What a smart machine, a *Chassidishe* Xerox machine that can copy the *Shaar HaYichud*! No: it has no idea what it says there. All it copied over were the shapes of the letters. The same with a JPEG or a GIF of the book fed into a computer, or this very class, fed into a computer, up onto the site and down into another computer, and people say, "Wow, the computers are smart: the computer is giving over the whole *Shaar HaYichud*."
blocks.outOfPlace: Added in the review at the end of the next class (226); the tape ends here.

sections.title: In speech the feeling becomes a separate yesh, sefira by sefira
sections.summary: Brought out in speech, a feeling becomes a thing apart, a *yesh* of a *yesh*, that can travel across the country and across time. The *Malchus* of each *sefira*, down to the particulars, becomes that *sefira* of *Malchus*: the anger a man wants to express is the anger heard in his voice.

phrases.he: כך בחינת התגלות העצמיות שבמדה שבלב, כשבאה בבחינת התגלות יש בדבור בה' מוצאות הפה נעשה בבחינת יש נבדל בפני עצמו,
שנקרא יש דיש,
phrases.en: It's a something of a something.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: So too the attribute in the heart: come out in speech, it becomes a *yesh nivdal*, a separate thing by itself. That is why the voice can travel to Los Angeles while the speaker stays here, and writing travels over time: the Rebbe's letters came to us as a thing by itself, like this book. It is *yesh d'yesh*, **a something of a something**: in the Rebbe's own thought, in the *Malchus* of the *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*, it was already a *yesh*; where *Malchus* is built by itself, it is a *yesh* of a *yesh*.

phrases.he: וכמו בחינת חכמה שבחסד שבלב הבא בגלוי באופן מוגבל, הרי עדיין אחוז ומתאחד בעצם החכמה והחסד כו' אבל גלוי שלו בדבור, שזהו כמו מאמר יהי אור,
הוא מהות דבר נבדל בפני עצמו,
phrases.en: That's already a totally separate thing.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת חכמה שבחסד דמלכות שנמשך מבחינת מלכות דחכממה דחסד שבזעיר אנפין בדרך פרט
וכך הוא כל בנין פרטים
phrases.en: And it's like that in all the different *pratim*.

phrases.he: דעשר ספירות דמלכות באורות וכלים בפרצוף בפני עצמו כו'

blocks.text: *Chachma* within *chesed* in the heart, even revealed in a limited way, is still bound up with the essence of the *chachma* and the *chesed*. Its revelation in speech, like the saying "Let there be light", is **already a totally separate thing**. It is *chachma* within *chesed* of *Malchus*, from the *Malchus* of *chachma* within *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin*: in the particulars too, not only does the *Malchus* of *chesed* become the *chesed* of *Malchus*, but the *Malchus* of *chachma* within *chesed* becomes *chachma* within *chesed* of *Malchus*.

**And it's like that in all the different *pratim***, the first order of *sefiros*, the second or the third: from the *Malchus* of the *sefira* comes the *sefira* of *Malchus*, and from the *Malchus* of the *sefira* of the *sefira* comes the *sefira* of the *sefira* of *Malchus*.

blocks.title: Love and anger in the voice
blocks.text: It hardly needs explaining. When a person feels love and wants to express it, from that comes the love within the speech. The same with hate or anger. He says, "You! What did you do?" Where does that come from? Not just from his being angry, but from his wanting to express the anger. The anger went from its *Chabad*, the reason for it, through *Chagas*, the feeling of it, through *Nehi*, its *hispaalus*, all the way to its *Malchus*: the anger was already a *yesh*, trying to come out of him. That *Malchus* of the anger became the anger in the speech: you hear that the man is angry, in the voice and in the words.

The same with *chachma*. When *chachma* or *bina* want to express themselves, people say, "Wow, that was a really smart speech." Where did that come from? The *chachma* of *Malchus* came from the *Malchus* of *chachma*. It is a simple thing. And so the whole structure of the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* is built, a vessel and *partzuf* of its own.

sections.title: Before the sawing a tail; then a point that falls silent
sections.summary: Before the *nesira* *Malchus* was the back of each *sefira* of *Zeir Anpin*, with no being of its own. To be built it first becomes a point: to speak well one must first not speak, and think. Then people listen.

phrases.he: וקודם הנסירה היו ד"ו פרצופין, שכמו האחוריים שנגרר אחר הפנים, בלתי מהות בפני עצמו כך בבחינת אחוריים דכל ספירה היה נכלל בחינת התגלות דמלכות, כי יש בכלל מאתיים כו'
(וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בפרטים ענין אחור באחור ואחור בפנים כו'
ומאן דאמר זנב היה כו')
phrases.en: It was a tail.

blocks.text: Before the *nesira* there were two faces joined: *Malchus* was like the back that is dragged along behind the face, with no being of its own. So in the back of each *sefira* was included the revelation of *Malchus*: within each *sefira* is the wish to express itself and be a something. It is included automatically.

blocks.title: Two ways to write a tzadik
blocks.text: It is like the letter *tzadik*: there are two ways to write it, *achor b'achor* (back to back) and *achor b'fanim* (back to face), with the woman's face at the back. Back to back, he faces forward and she faces backward. Back to face, she faces forward too, looking at his back: she sees nothing but a brick wall, like those tenements where you open the window onto a brick wall. And another opinion says **it was a tail**. These are not necessarily exclusive: *Malchus* is a tail of each *sefira*.

phrases.he: ומתחלה היא נקודה תחת יסוד זעיר אנפין כו', כמו שכתוב ותפול לפני רגליו, וכמו שכתוב בזהר על פסוק עושי דברו,
אזעירת גרמה כנקודה
phrases.en: She made herself small like a *nekuda*.

phrases.he: כו' עד ה"א כמלקדמין
phrases.en: Till it becomes a *hei* just like the *hei* that was before.

blocks.text: At first she is a *nekuda* (point) under the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, like a *chirik* under a *yud*, as it says "she fell before his feet", of Esther and Achashverosh. And the *Zohar* says on "those who do His word": **she made herself small like a *nekuda***. That means that to talk properly, first of all you have to make the talk *batel* (nullified) and go into the thinking.

blocks.title: The spontaneous speech
blocks.text: Someone can get up and make a speech spontaneously, but only if he already knows the subject very well: the going into it, into *bina*, happened earlier. That is why he can speak now. To fall at his feet and be a point under the *yud* means: in order to speak, he has to not speak.

As they say, a *meshugener* (madman) says what he thinks, and a wise man thinks what he says. When someone says everything right away, and the speech never becomes a point, it ends up just baloney and babble: there is no *binyan* (structure).
For a proper structure of *Malchus*, *Malchus* first has to make itself small, actually a nothing. In order finally to speak, a person has to sit there without speaking.

You know the people everybody wants to avoid? Usually it is because they want to speak all the time and don't know what they are saying, until you just want to say, "Get away from me," and wonder how to get rid of this person. Right away they want to speak, and in the end nobody wants to listen to them: the whole purpose of the speech is not fulfilled.
The whole purpose of speech is that people should listen to you. That is why it is called *Malchus*: the whole point of a king is that they have to listen to him. You don't want just to talk.

The craziest type of person is the one who walks around the street just talking to himself. He needs to talk so much that he doesn't even care whether anybody is listening, and nobody is. It happens because he never stops the talking in order to think.

sensitivity.reason: Calls a man who walks the street talking to himself "the craziest type of person"; it can read as mockery of the mentally ill.

blocks.title: When E.F. Hutton talks
blocks.text: The more a person stops talking to think, the wiser he is, and then people want to listen, because they know that what he says will be arranged by proper thought. There used to be an advertisement: "When E.F. Hutton talks, everybody listens." (A listener offers Alan Greenspan instead; that works too, but this was the advertisement.) Why do they listen? Because he sat there, analyzed the whole situation and figured it out, and he will give you good advice: before he talked, he thought. That is the strange thing about *dibur* (speech): it begins *davka* by not talking, by becoming a nothing.

She makes herself small like a point, a total nothing, **till it becomes a *hei* just like the *hei* that was before**, like *bina*. The lower *hei* becomes a point and lets the thing go up to the upper *hei*, until it is just like it, and then everybody will listen.

sections.title: Face to face, and the speech practiced before the mirror
sections.summary: Made small, *Malchus* rises to the upper *hei* and stands face to face with *Zeir Anpin*. Its building in *Atzilus* is a speech fully written inside; beyond that, the *Malchus* of *Malchus*, practiced before the mirror, breaks through the screen and becomes a *partzuf* in *Beriya*, the effect on the listeners.

phrases.he: שאחר כך נבנית בפרצוף בבחינת האצילות
עד שנעשית בבחינת פנים בפנים כו'
phrases.en: Till it becomes *panim b'panim*.

phrases.he: כדמיון מיעוט הירח ומלוי הירח
phrases.en: Like the moon that gets empty and full.

blocks.text: Afterwards she is built into a *partzuf* in *Atzilus*, until she is *panim b'panim* (face to face): now she is further in than he is. *Zeir Anpin* looks inward, toward *bina*. *Malchus*, having made herself small, is now like the upper *hei*, on the level of *bina*, where he was looking; so it is face to face, **like the moon that gets empty and full**.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר ענין בנין המלכות, שהוא למעלה מבנין המלכות בפרצוף בבי"ע,
phrases.en: This is the *inyan* of the *binyan hamalchus* in *Atzilus*, which is higher than the *binyan hamalchus*, the *partzuf* in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*.

phrases.he: שנסתר כל פרצופה שבבחינת אצילות, עד בחינת מלכות דמלכות שבוקע המסך ונעשית בבחינת פרצוף בבריאה, כמו שיתבאר כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: This is a higher thing: the building of *Malchus* in *Atzilus*, which is higher than the building of *Malchus* as a *partzuf* in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, where her whole *partzuf* of *Atzilus* is hidden, down to the *Malchus* of *Malchus*, which breaks through the *masach* (screen) and becomes a *partzuf* in *Beriya*.

blocks.title: The speech written and ready
blocks.text: There are two things here. One: in *Atzilus* itself she has to make herself small for the full building of *Malchus*. In terms of speech, the man writing a speech builds it up until it is all arranged and perfectly ready to say. But he has not said it yet: it has not gone through to the receiver, to the outside, to *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, the *alma d'peruda* (world of separation), where you are already talking to somebody else. It is all still inside him. The other: for that, the whole inner *Malchus* has to disappear and leave only the *Malchus* of *Malchus*, the letters. That is why he goes over the speech almost to memorize it, so that it is *shagur al leshono* (fluent on his tongue).

blocks.title: Practicing before the mirror
blocks.text: To back up a little: the building of *Malchus* in *Atzilus* is that he has built the whole speech inside himself, written within him. Even then he is not ready to give it perfectly, because it is still all its ten *sefiros*, and now he needs the building of *Malchus* of *Malchus*, with ten *sefiros* too. So he stands and practices, in front of a mirror, or he tells his wife, "Here, listen to me." He goes over not just what he will say but which part he will stress and where he will talk low, and watches how he will make a sweep with his hands.

blocks.text: From the built *Malchus* he already knows the emotion he wants to get across: a speech of *chesed*; or, if he is a rabble-rouser, getting everybody angry; or making everybody feel kind and merciful so they will give money to the poor orphans with the patches in their yarmulkes. Still he practices in front of the mirror, to make sure that the *sefiros* of *Malchus* transfer properly to the *sefiros* of *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

It is the same rule: from the *Malchus* of a *sefira* comes the *sefira* of *Malchus*, so from *Malchus* of *chesed* of *Malchus* comes *chesed* of *Malchus* of *Malchus*. In the built speech there is *chesed* of *Malchus*, a feeling of love he wants to convey; *gevura* of *Malchus*, anger and hatred; *tiferes* of *Malchus*, mercy, compassion. Within that is the wish to convey it into the actual letters when he speaks. That is the building of *Malchus* of *Malchus*, how it will go through to be *Keser* of *Beriya*: when he speaks to his audience, he should get the effect he wants in their *taanug* (delight) and *ratzon* (will), and move them as he wants, to give money, or to storm the Bastille, or the other person to love him back.

So there are two things: the building of *Malchus* itself in *Atzilus*, and then the whole *partzuf* of *Atzilus* hidden down to *Malchus* of *Malchus*, which breaks through the *masach* and becomes a *partzuf* in *Beriya*, with ten *sefiros* of its own. That is what he practices: that when the speech actually comes out of his mouth and breaks through the screen, it is the *partzuf* he wanted. Otherwise a mistake can happen: he wanted to convey a feeling, he did not practice properly, and it does not come across. He is not a good speaker. He also wants people to listen, to say, "Wow, what a speaker," and to do what he says.

That is *Malchus*: he wants to be the king. The rabble-rouser wants the people to listen to him and storm the Bastille. The same with intellect: he may want to convey an idea to a class. This is *Beriya*: he is making a new creation over there, a mood, and they say of the speaker, "Wow." That is how the *Malchus* of *Malchus* becomes a *partzuf* in *Beriya*, as later chapters will discuss.

sections.title: The large dalet of echad: built by Abba and Ima and sent out to rule
sections.summary: The large *dalet* of *echad* is *Malchus* fully built in *Atzilus*; the small *dalet* is its *Malchus* breaking through the screen. *Chachma* and *bina* build it from the *Malchus* of the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin* and send it out to rule, for a king rules by his word, and the power of speech stays in *Zeir Anpin* even when he is silent.

phrases.he: והנה זהו באמת ענין דלית רבתי דאחד,
phrases.en: This is the real *inyan* of *dalet ravrevsa d'echad*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת גדלות פרצוף נוקבא דזעיר אנפין בבחינת האצילות, דוקא במוחין ומדות, אורות וכלים

blocks.question: Wasn't the large dalet of echad said to be even before the tzimtzum, and then to be tevuna? How is this the real one?
blocks.text: **This is the real *inyan* of *dalet ravrevsa d'echad***: it is the greatness of the *partzuf* of the *Nukva* of *Zeir Anpin* in *Atzilus*, *davka* with *mochin* and *middos*, lights and vessels. The large *dalet* is *Malchus* as it is in *Atzilus*; the little *dalet* is the *Malchus* of *Malchus* breaking through the *masach*.

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב ויבן יהו״ה אלהי״ם את הצלע,
שהוא אבא ואמא דאצילות, דבנו לה כו'
phrases.en: She was built by *chachma* and *bina*.

phrases.he: ואמרו לה זילי נטירי ביתך,
phrases.en: Go and take care of your house.

phrases.he: להיות ראש לבי"ע כו')
phrases.en: Now go out and be the head for *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*.

phrases.he: (כידוע בענין באר חפרוה שרים כו')

blocks.text: "And *Havaya Elokim* built the rib": *Abba* and *Ima* of *Atzilus* built her. **She was built by *chachma* and *bina***: *Havaya* is *chachma* and *Elokim* is *bina*. The rib is the material, the *Malchus* of *Zeir Anpin*, the *middos* she was taken from; but she is built from higher than the *Malchus* of *Zeir Anpin*, by *chachma* and *bina*.

They build her up and then tell her, **Go and take care of your house**: **now go out and be the head for *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya***. The intellect builds the speech out of the *middos*, out of the *Malchus* of *Zeir Anpin*, and then tells her to go outside and be the head of all of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*. On "as is known of the well the princes dug": apparently there is some *inyan* in *Kabbala* on this verse.

phrases.he: והענין הוא דבחינת דבור שבמחשבה הנזכר לעיל, שזהו ד' רבתי, נעשה מחשבה שבדבור העליון דזעיר אנפין בבחינת עשר ספירות אורות וכלים,
שהוא ממלכות דט׳ ספירות דזעיר אנפין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: The *inyan* of *Malchus* is coming from the *Malchus* of the ten *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: והיינו א"ח ד',
phrases.en: Nine: from the nine comes the *Malchus*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות
וכמו שכתוב ויהי האדם לנפש חיה, רוח ממללא,
phrases.en: The *adam* became a speaking spirit.

phrases.he: שהוא דבר מלך שלטון
phrases.en: The word of the king is the rule.

phrases.he: בי' מאמרות ויאמר אלהי״ם כו' כידוע

blocks.text: The speech in thought, the large *dalet*, becomes the thought within the upper speech of *Zeir Anpin*, ten *sefiros*, lights and vessels: *Malchus* comes from the *Malchus* of the *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*. That is the nine and the *dalet*: from the nine comes the *Malchus*. As it says, "and man became a living soul, a speaking spirit": **the *adam* became a speaking spirit**.

**The word of the king is the rule**: the rule of a king comes *davka* through his words. If a king only thinks something, he cannot complain when it is not done; if he says it and you don't do it, it is a death penalty. That is the rule of the king.

blocks.title: The depth of the Megillah
blocks.text: We are coming up to Purim, and you see how deep the Megillah is. You think it is just telling a story, but all of it, that she fell at his feet and all that business, and "the word of the king is the rule", that what came out from the king and was sealed with the king's ring cannot go back and has to be done: all these are matters of *Malchus*. In fact the whole second half of *Shaarei Orah* is on the matters of Purim. The king's horse and the king's garment, putting Mordechai on the horse the king rode, in the king's clothes and the king's crown: you think it is a wonderful kiddie story, and really it is all deep stuff. It is called *Megillas Esther*, the revealing of the hidden. And the word of the king is the rule in the ten sayings, "And *Elokim* said": when He said it, it had to be done.

phrases.he: ובחינת כתר דמלכות דאצילות הוא בחינת כח הדבור טרם שמתפשט לדבר,
phrases.en: That's the *hiyuli* power of speaking, before he even thinks of speaking.

phrases.he: בבחינת שכל ומדות שבדבור, שהוא ט׳ ספירות דמלכות
והיינו ענין לעולם יהו״ה דברך נצב בשמים, בחינת זעיר אנפין,
דהיינו בחינת כח הדבור שדבוק בחזה דזעיר אנפין תמיד כו',
phrases.en: In the *chazeh*, the *koach hadibur* is there even when you don't speak.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בעץ חיים ומבואר במקום אחר

blocks.text: *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the power of speech before it spreads into speaking, intellect and *middos* in the speech. So *Keser* here is relative to *Malchus*: **the *hiyuli* power of speaking, before he even thinks of speaking**. That is "Forever, *Havaya*, Your word stands in the heavens", in *Zeir Anpin*: the power of speech always cleaves to the *chazeh* (chest) of *Zeir Anpin*, and there it is even when you don't speak.

sections.title: Dalet and dal: Malchus has nothing of its own
sections.summary: *Malchus* clothes the four *middos* of *Tanhi*, only their final decision, so it is a *dalet*; and it is *dal*, poor, with nothing of its own. Its root is *chesed*, the mood in which a person wants to talk, and it shines like the moon, until the time to come when the speech is as great as the thought.

phrases.he: והתפשטות המלכות מלבשת לתנה"י דזעיר אנפין,
שהוא בחינת דלי"ת,
phrases.en: That's why it's called *dalet*.

phrases.he: והמלכות נקרא דל
phrases.en: It's also called *dal* because she's small, low, poor.

blocks.text: The spreading of *Malchus* clothes *Tanhi* (*tiferes*, *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Zeir Anpin*: **that's why it's called *dalet***. It does not clothe the *etzem* of the *middos*, *chesed* and *gevura*. *Tiferes* is also called mercy, which means the connection with the other person: to give something over to another, you need a connection with him, and that is where speech comes from. And *Malchus* can clothe only the *hachraa* (decision), not the first choice between *chesed* and *gevura*.

*Nehi* is easy: it is not the *etzem* of the *middos* but their *hispaalus*, so *Malchus* clothes it. The hard part is *tiferes*: why *Tanhi* and not just *Nehi*? Because it does carry the *etzem* of the *middos*, but not as they are, only their final *hachraa*: not the first *hataya* between *chesed* and *gevura*, where each is full, but after they are mixed. So it clothes four *middos*, and is called *dalet*. **It's also called *dal* because she's small, low, poor**: she has nothing of her own, and like a poor person has to beg for everything from others.

phrases.he: ושרש בנין המלכות מחסדים דזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: The *shoresh* of the *binyan hamalchus* is from the *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב והוכן בחסד כסאו,
phrases.en: The *kisei*, the *Malchus*, is *muchan davka* in *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכתיב אשרי משכיל אל דל,
וחסד ח"ס דלי"ת,
phrases.en: *Chesed* means he's *chas* on the poor person.

phrases.he: דהמלכות לית לה מגרמה כלום,
phrases.en: has nothing from itself,

phrases.he: רק מה שמקבלת מזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: only whatever it receives from *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בענין התגלות דהתגלות כו',
phrases.en: A revelation of a revelation.

phrases.he: כמשל הלבנה שמקבת מאור השמש,
וכמו שכתוב בזהר דסיהרא לית לה מגרמה כו'
phrases.en: The moon has no light of its own.

blocks.text: **The *shoresh* of the *binyan hamalchus* is from the *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin***: *Malchus*, speech, comes *davka* from *chesed*, which is spreading out.

blocks.title: "What is it?" "Nothing."
blocks.text: That is why a person wants to talk *davka* when he is happy and loving; when he is angry he usually doesn't want to talk. You go to your wife and ask, "What is it?" and she says, "Nothing," and "Don't you want to talk about it?" "Nope." When somebody doesn't want to talk about it, it means they're angry. When someone is loving and kind, he is in an expansive mood, and then he wants to talk.

sensitivity.reason: A husband-and-wife joke: the wife who answers "Nothing" when she is angry.

blocks.question: Didn't we say the building of Malchus was from chachma and bina?
blocks.text: Yes: *chachma* and *bina* are the ones who actually build it, and the materials come from the *Malchus* of the nine *sefiros*. But the *shoresh* (root) of the building comes from the *chasadim* of *Zeir Anpin*, and you see it: a person wants to talk *davka* from the *chasadim*.

As it says, "His throne is established in *chesed*": **the *kisei*, the *Malchus*, is *muchan davka* in *chesed***. And "Happy is he who is wise toward the *dal*": *chesed* is *chas dalet*; *chesed* means **he's *chas* on the poor person**. *Malchus* has nothing from itself, only what it receives from *Zeir Anpin*: a revelation of a revelation, like the moon that receives from the light of the sun, as the *Zohar* says, **the moon has no light of its own**.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשזעיר אנפין ונוקבא היו שוין בקומתן כמו שהיו קודם מיעוט הירח, שנקרא שני מאורות הגדולים,
phrases.en: It's not like that when they were equal.

phrases.he: וכן לעתיד לבא דכתיב והיה אור הלבנה כו'

blocks.text: **It's not like that when they were equal**, before the moon was diminished, when both were called the great lights; and so in the time to come, when "the light of the moon will be" like the sun. Then the speech will be just as big as the thought. This is when a person becomes a *talmid chacham* who learns his *girsa*, *davka* speaking the Torah, and then it becomes even higher.

sections.title: Two buildings of the Nukva: the head of the foxes, and the night
sections.summary: The *Nukva* is built twice: in *Atzilus*, by the *nesira*, and again as the head of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*. There she makes herself less, the head of foxes instead of the tail of lions, and rules the night of the world of separation.

phrases.he: אך יש ב' מדריגות גם בבנין הנוקבא, הא' בבחינת האצילות שהוא ענין הנסירה כו', והב' מה שנעשית ראש לבי"ע
(והוא מה שכתוב במקום אחר בענין לכי ומעטי את עצמך כו',
phrases.en: Make yourself less.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת המלכות שנעשית ראש לשועלים בבי"ע,
phrases.en: Instead of becoming the tail of the lions, it becomes the head of the foxes.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ואת המאור הקטן לממשלת הלילה
ובכלל כל בחינת האצילות נקרא יום,
phrases.en: In general the *bechina* of *Atzilus* is called day.

phrases.he: ומדת לילה הוא בחינת המלכות כשמסתתרת בראש הבריאה, כמו שיתבאר בסמוך בענין ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד כו', אחר בקיעת המסך כו' ודי למבין)

blocks.text: There are two levels in building the *Nukva*: one in *Atzilus*, the *nesira*, and the second, that she becomes the head of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, as discussed earlier. This is "Go and make yourself less", to go into *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*: **instead of becoming the tail of the lions, it becomes the head of the foxes**, "the lesser light to rule the night".

**In general the *bechina* of *Atzilus* is called day**; *Malchus* hidden in the head of *Beriya*, gone into the *alma d'peruda*, is the night. So the chapter has spoken of the *nesira*, the building of *Malchus* in *Atzilus*, and then the building of *Malchus* for action.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between the *tzelem* and the *dmus*, and in what way does it make no difference, and in what way does it?
How does the *Malchus* of anger in a person become the anger heard in his speech?
Why must *Malchus* first become a point under *Zeir Anpin* before it can be built, and what does this teach about a person who wants to be listened to?
What are the two buildings of *Malchus*, and how does practicing a speech before a mirror show the second?
Why is *Malchus* called *dalet* and *dal*, and why is its root in *chesed*?
